title: Edmund and the Oath
premise: Lena Blackwood, an exiled storm-caller, hides among charm-sellers in the city of Vell until the crown's witch-hunt forces her to flee toward the Grey Door, the last passage out of a kingdom that erased her homeland from its maps. She is joined by Edmund, a disgraced oath-keeper who once swore to protect her family and has spent five years atoning for his failure, and together they gather other hunted magicians into an unlikely caravan. Betrayed by one of their own and cornered by the king's hunters in the frozen pass, Lena must finally embrace the storm she has suppressed since exile—knowing it may cost her the belonging she has only just found. In the end she holds the Door open long enough for the others to escape, and Edmund renews his broken oath not to protect her, but to walk beside her into whatever country they build next.
about_author: Orsen Yarrow is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade drawing borders that no longer matched the ground beneath them. They write about people who belong to places that have been erased.

chapters.title: Charms for a City Without Magic
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In outlawed Vell, Lena sells harmless trinkets while hiding her storm-gift behind careful routines and a forged identity. When royal criers announce a hunt for anyone with the gift, her neighbor is dragged away in chains. Emotional beat: the fragile safety of invisibility shatters; fear becomes resolve.

chapters.title: The Man Who Knew Her Name
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Preparing to flee alone, Lena is ambushed by Edmund, an oath-keeper who guarded her family before the fall of their homeland—and who let her go into exile rather than die beside them. He offers to guide her to the Grey Door. Emotional beat: resentment wrestling with hunger for connection.

chapters.title: What the Maps Forgot
chapters.summary: Dual POV, alternating. Fleeing through countryside where her homeland's name has been scraped from every signpost, Lena and Edmund argue about the past while evading hunter patrols. They rescue Tam, a frightened child whose small gift flares when he cries. Emotional beat: the first stitch of found family.

chapters.title: The Hearth Beneath the Hill
chapters.summary: Tam's POV, close third. The trio shelters with a hidden community of gifted folk led by Maren, a healer who has chosen hiding over flight. Lena is offered sanctuary—but staying means burying her power forever, as Maren did. Emotional beat: warmth that feels suspiciously like a cage.

chapters.title: An Oath Is a Kind of Wound
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. By firelight, Edmund confesses the full truth: he broke his oath by obeying orders to stand down during the massacre of Lena's kin. Lena cannot forgive him yet, but the caravan gains three more refugees, including Sef, a charming illusionist who volunteers to scout ahead. Emotional beat: guilt laid bare; trust tentatively extended.

chapters.title: The Hunter Who Smiles
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef meets secretly with Captain Ives, the hunt's smiling commander—he has been selling the caravan's route all along. Meanwhile Lena discovers her storm-gift growing stronger near the mountains, dangerous and exhilarating. Emotional beat: dramatic irony tightens; the reader knows what the family does not.

chapters.title: Snowfall on the Broken Road
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The long winter falls early. Sef's false scouting report leads the group into a box canyon where Ives waits with soldiers. Edmund takes a crossbow bolt meant for Tam; Maren's healing can't reach them here. Emotional beat: betrayal revealed, the found family bloodied but unbroken.

chapters.title: Let It Fall
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, climax part one. Cornered above the pass, Lena stops suppressing herself and calls the storm she has feared for five years—lightning splits the canyon, scattering Ives's men, but the wild magic nearly kills Tam before Edmund shields him with his body. Emotional beat: identity embraced at terrible cost; power and love colliding.

chapters.title: The Grey Door
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax part two. At the Door—a seam of old magic in a glacier wall—Ives makes a final stand. Edmund formally releases his broken oath and swears a new one: to stand beside Lena, not between her and the world. She holds the Door open against the storm while everyone passes through. Emotional beat: forgiveness as an act of will; sacrifice without martyrdom.

chapters.title: A Country Not Yet Named
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, resolution. On the far side, the refugees camp in a green valley beyond any king's reach. Maren arrives having abandoned her hiding place; even Ives lets them go, unsettled by what he witnessed. Lena plants a boundary stone with no name on it yet. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not granted; a future left open like a door.
